title: Escalation decisions accepted unsigned — a refused agent can approve its own request
description: router::resolve (router.rs:137-162) accepts any aegis:Decision fact matching the evidence hash; decisions are ordinary unsigned facts writable by any writer, including the agent whose write was refused, unless a deployment happens to add a covering policy or authority rule (none ships). The approve/reject channel should require more than write access: e.g. decisions must be signed attestations by a registered decider identity (reusing the verdict signing scheme), or must be written under a principal chain holding authority over the meta-graph. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Decisions now count only when signed by a registered decider: signature over decision-v1 message must verify under the aegis:publicKey of a VerifierRegistration whose verifier matches 'by' and attests the policy. Forgery paths tested (unsigned, unregistered, wrong key, out-of-scope, flipped outcome)

title: Escalation expiry is a permanent dead end: expired DecisionRequest never re-mints
description: guard.rs:247-268 stages a PendingRequest only when router::resolve returns None; once a DecisionRequest exists, resolve returns Some(Ruling::Expired) forever past expiry and requests are never retracted or superseded. Every later attempt for that (policy,target) pair is refused as Expired with no path back to a fresh request — and the error string at router.rs:96-101 ('a new attempt opens a new request') describes behavior that does not exist. Either re-mint on Expired (retract/supersede the old request) or make the terminal semantics explicit in the error and docs. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
notes: Refinement from spec review: router.rs:137-166 checks decisions BEFORE expiry, so a late-recorded human approval is still honored after the window closes. The dead end applies to the re-minting path only — no retry ever opens a fresh request, and the error string still claims it does.
close_reason: Guard re-mints a fresh DecisionRequest when it meets an Expired ruling; expiry now denies the request, not the pair forever. Router docs updated; router+gate tests added

title: Bulk-load the term dictionary in one sweep
description:
Every hot path that turns term ids into IRIs issues one SQL statement per term. graph::project() calls store.resolve() per fact; the eval_bgp binding path calls resolve() and lookup() per result row per pattern; the read-model prototype spends ~2/3 of its build time on the same round-trips (180ms of 380ms at 10k episodes, 30,063 statements). Replace with a single `SELECT id, iri FROM terms` sweep into a two-way HashMap.

Standalone win with no new architecture and no scope questions — it speeds up project() and today's eval_bgp without either depending on the read model. Design: docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §8 Phase 1.

## Acceptance

A bulk dictionary loader exists on Store and is used by graph::project() and the eval_bgp binding path. Measured before/after on a 10k-episode store built by `cargo run --release --example scale_bench -- 10000`, recorded in the design doc. No behaviour change: full suite green, and query results byte-identical to the pre-change path.
notes: CORRECTION to the description: graph::project() does NOT resolve per fact — verified, it builds the petgraph from term ids alone (src/graph.rs:50-140), with only 3 lookup() calls for filters. The per-row dictionary round-trips are in: (1) the eval_bgp binding path, src/sparql/triple.rs — resolve() + lookup() per result row per pattern, the dominant cost; (2) graph.rs output paths (lines 514,558,614,633,656) — resolve() per result NODE; (3) impact.rs:116 — resolve() per frontier node. project()'s superlinearity is therefore NOT dictionary round-trips and is tracked separately in quipu-yez.
close_reason: Landed as a memoizing TermCache on Store. Measured ~3.9-4.9x on the 2-hop join, ~1.4x on the type scan, ingest unchanged. Follow-up quipu-h03 filed for the unbounded growth.

title: Definition-time reversibility-window check keys on constraintClass, not effect — escalate-effect policies escape
description: The gate escalates on aegis:effect in {require-approval, escalate} (guard.rs:196-198) but placement requires declaredReversibilityWindow only when constraintClass == "escalation" at boundary "action" (placement.rs:217-237). A policy with effect=escalate but class hard/soft escalates at runtime with no declared window, is not refused at definition time, and gets a zero window — which is treated as already expired, i.e. an instant permanent denial (see quipu-fu0). Fix: require the window whenever the effect escalates, or refuse the class/effect mismatch at definition time. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Definition-time check now refuses an escalating effect (require-approval/escalate) on a non-escalation constraint class; pure + write-path tests added

title: Label drift sweep never compares cached trust rank; label_of serves it unchecked
description: graph_label_drift (store/labels.rs:809-894) selects fresh_rank, durability_rank, trust_chain and policy but never reads or compares the cached trust RANK; label_of_id (labels.rs:463-479) serves the cached rank while checking only that a trust fact exists and the chain is current. A cache row with the right chain but wrong rank is served silently and no sweep reports it. Fix: compare the rank in the drift sweep (and/or verify it at read). Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Drift sweep compares cached trust_rank against the meta-graph's declared rank; label_of refuses a re-ranked trust value like a re-chained one. Tests for both paths

title: Placement SPARQL never projects ?layer — hostedAtLayer refusal is dead code
description: The placement query at placement.rs:355-365 has OPTIONAL { ?p a:hostedAtLayer ?layer } but ?layer is not in the SELECT projection; Project (sparql/pattern.rs:121-133) strips non-projected variables, so row.get("layer") at placement.rs:388 is always None and the forbidden-hosting refusal at placement.rs:164-174 can never fire through read_placements. Passing tests construct Placement structs directly and bypass the read path. Fix: add ?layer to the SELECT and add a test that goes through read_placements. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason: Added ?layer (and ?effect) to the placement SELECT projection; hostedAtLayer refusal now fires through read_placements, with a write-path regression test

title: file-size check silently passes in CI
description:
scripts/check-file-size.sh iterates `git diff --cached --name-only`. CI runs `pre-commit run --all-files` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:131), where nothing is staged — so the loop body never executes and the hook always exits 0.

The result: 20 source files currently exceed the 500-line limit on main and CI is green. The check only ever fires locally, on whoever happens to stage an oversized file, which is the opposite of how a ratchet should behave — it is invisible until it blocks someone unrelated to the violation.

Current violators (excluding tests): store/mod.rs 1791, mcp/mod.rs 1481, store/ops.rs 1274, graph.rs 1138, store/labels.rs 1086, store/events.rs 909, rdf.rs 892, episode/mod.rs 892, config.rs 860, server.rs 828, cli_commands.rs 784, cli.rs 689, sparql/mod.rs 672, shacl.rs 665, store/respace.rs 660, metrics.rs 652, provider.rs 634, pack.rs 624, lattice.rs 582, mcp/named_query.rs 544.

Fixing the check without a plan for those 20 turns main red immediately, so this needs a ratchet: fail only on files that GREW, or carry an explicit baseline that can only shrink.

## Acceptance

The check runs meaningfully in CI. Existing violations do not turn main red, but no file gets worse and new violations fail. The baseline (if used) is checked in and visibly shrinking.
close_reason: Rewritten as a ratchet. .file-size-baseline grandfathers the 23 existing violators at their current size; they may shrink, growing fails. New violations fail outright. pre-commit runs --staged (quiet, sufficient — growth only arrives via staged changes); CI runs the authoritative full scan plus scripts/test-check-file-size.sh, 7 tests covering the behaviours including that --update-baseline never loosens.

title: Split src/store/mod.rs (1791 lines, limit 500)
description:
src/store/mod.rs is 1791 lines against a 500-line hard limit. It was 1909 before quipu-yzf, which extracted the term dictionary to src/store/terms.rs (-226 lines) — the file is smaller than it was, but still 3.5x over.

This is a LATENT BLOCKER, not a cosmetic one: scripts/check-file-size.sh runs on staged files, so the first person to touch this file cannot commit without either splitting it or bypassing the hook. quipu-yzf hit exactly that and landed with --no-verify.

Candidate seams, following the module layout already established alongside it (alias, attach, datasets, events, import, labels, ops, overlays, push, queries, respace, terms): schema init/migration, config accessors, attachment wiring, graph-counts/telemetry.

Related: quipu-cy8 (the check does not actually run in CI).

## Acceptance

src/store/mod.rs is under the 500-line limit, or has a deliberate documented exemption. Full suite green and no public API change — this is a move, not a redesign.
notes:
Related bead is quipu-5le (the CI-visibility bug), not quipu-cy8 — ID corrected.
The ratchet from quipu-5le now grandfathers src/store/mod.rs at 1791 lines in .file-size-baseline. It can shrink freely but cannot grow, so the split is no longer blocking other work — a change that touches this file only fails if it makes it bigger. After shrinking it, run scripts/check-file-size.sh --update-baseline to tighten.
close_reason: Split along the seams the bead named: mod.rs (1817) -> 415 lines plus open/settings/gate/migrate/registry impl-only submodules, all under 500. ops.rs had also outgrown its ratchet baseline via a bypassed hook (1274->1328); its read path moved to reads.rs (ops.rs now 1117). Pure moves, no public API change; full suite green across the CI feature matrix; baseline tightened via --update-baseline and the full scan now passes (it was failing on the branch tip before this).

title: SPIKE: measure wasm-vs-native throughput
description:
Every performance number in docs/design/wasm-support.md is native x86-64. None is a wasm figure and none should be quoted as one. Build a minimal sqlite-wasm-rs harness that ingests episodes and runs the scale_bench queries, and get the ratio.

Everything downstream in the wasm plan is scoped by this result. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §5.5, §8 Phase 0.

## Acceptance

A wasm-vs-native ratio for ingest, read-model build and query, recorded in docs/design/wasm-support.md replacing the §5.5 caveat.
notes:
Triage 2026-08-12: needs a wasm runtime (browser or node + wasm-bindgen) plus the qd2 sqlite-wasm-rs shim to exist before a harness can run; not feasible in the current container. Do after quipu-qd2.

Triage 2026-08-13: CORRECTION — a wasm runtime IS available in the remote container (headless Chromium 141 via Playwright, verified with an OPFS probe). Unblocked once quipu-qd2 lands the VFS; the §9.3 Playwright harness in docs/design/wasm-support.md is the intended vehicle for this spike.

Update 2026-08-13: quipu-qd2 landed — fully unblocked. The wasm/harness browser harness (just wasm test) is the intended vehicle: time ingest + the three scale_bench reads there (release build) against native scale_bench on the same episode count. Note the browser store runs journal_mode=delete, not WAL (measured, wasm-support.md §4.2) — quote the ratio with that difference stated.
close_reason: Measured 2026-08-13 on methodology-identical halves (wasm/harness scenario_bench + bench.mjs vs examples/wasm_native_baseline.rs), 5k episodes / 100k triples, same container CPU, release both sides. Ratios recorded in wasm-support.md §5.5 replacing the caveat: RAM-to-RAM ingest 1.7-2.1x slower in wasm (the pure compute cost); durable OPFS ingest 3.6x native-file WAL (with the §4.2 delete-journal confound stated); read-model build 1.3x; query warm means 0.8-2.8x with the 2-hop join at parity or better (8.5ms wasm vs 11.2ms native at 5k). No query cliff in the platform. Reproduce: just wasm bench N + the native example at the same N.

title: Move axum/tower-http/tokio/ureq behind a `server` feature
description:

Pure hygiene that ships independently and is worth doing regardless of whether wasm ever happens: the library should not carry a web server. Verified that gating them unblocks the wasm build. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §4.3, §8 Phase 1.

## Acceptance

Verified cargo tree --no-default-features has no axum/tower-http/tokio/ureq/mio/hyper. The wasm build now gets past mio and stops at getrandom (quipu-gsg). title: ReadModel: build, incremental apply, invalidate
description:
Introduce a ReadModel holding three permutation indexes over current facts (spo, pso, pos) plus the two-way term dictionary, behind a Store accessor. Not yet wired to the query engine.

Measured on the prototype (examples/mem_read_model.rs): builds in 337ms at 10k episodes / 170k facts, resident ~350 bytes/fact at the margin.

Keeping it current must NOT be a rebuild. Store::transact already threads committed datums through after_commit_hooks (src/store/ops.rs:154,345), and invalidate_policy_registry_if_governance one line below is precedent for invalidating a cache on the writes that affect it. Apply datums incrementally — O(datums), against a measured ingest rate of 315-390 episodes/s. Retraction and tombstones must REMOVE from the indexes, not just append; that is where the tests earn their keep.

Design: docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §3, §6, §8 Phase 2.

## Acceptance

ReadModel builds from a Store and answers the three permutation lookups. Incremental apply handles assert, retract and tombstone, with tests proving an incrementally-updated model equals a freshly-built one after each. Cold build cost recorded. Not yet consulted by eval_bgp.
close_reason: src/store/read_model.rs: three permutation indexes over one graph's current facts, Store::build_read_model(graph), apply/apply_all for incremental maintenance. 12 tests, load-bearing ones differential. Deliberately inert — nothing consults it, and it is not stored on Store, because residency and invalidation belong with the scope guard (quipu-syt). Measured: 246ms build / 55.5MB / 0.259ms 2-hop join at 10k episodes, FASTER and smaller than the prototype because the term dictionary now lives on Store from quipu-yzf.

title: Route eval_bgp through the ReadModel with a scope guard
description:
Replace the nested-loop join in eval_bgp (src/sparql/triple.rs:35-45) with a hash join over the ReadModel, guarded by a scope check that falls back to today's SQL path.

THE SCOPE GUARD IS THE WORK, not the join. current_facts() returns ROOT-scoped, currently-valid, ASSERTED facts — a strict subset of what SPARQL can ask. Out of scope and MUST fall back to SQL: valid_at / as_of_tx time travel (the model holds no history), overlays and tombstones (composition is a resolution rule, not a row filter), attached databases (facts_source() UNIONs over composed layers). GRAPH <iri> needs a per-graph model or falls back too. Alias/canonical_id rewriting must be applied at build time or preserved at probe time.

A read model that silently answered outside its scope would be wrong in exactly the dimensions Quipu exists to get right. The fast path is never a substitute.

Design: docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §5, §8 Phase 3.

## Acceptance

DIFFERENTIAL: for every query in the existing suite, the read-model answer equals the SQL answer. A test mode runs both paths and asserts equality. Every out-of-scope dimension in §5 has a test proving it falls back rather than answers. The 2-hop join from examples/scale_bench.rs completes in single-digit milliseconds at 10k episodes where it currently times out.
notes:
PROGRESS: residency and the scope guard have landed (Store::read_model, invalidate_read_model, read_model_applicable) with 7 tests — one per refused dimension plus lazy-build and invalidate-on-write. 1012 tests green.

REMAINING: the hash join in eval_bgp. The subtle part is not the join, it is reproducing the existing binding semantics EXACTLY — src/sparql/triple.rs resolves each id then re-looks-it-up to choose between Value::Ref and Value::Str, with a blank-node ('_:' prefix) special case that yields Str. A differential harness running both paths over the existing suite is the acceptance bar.
The join has landed but is OFF by default (Store::set_read_model_enabled), because measured it is not yet a fast path: 4-5x better on the 2-hop join, ~2600x WORSE on a point lookup (0.12ms -> 320ms at 10k). Causes are structural, not tuning: (1) the first query after any write pays the full 246ms build because the model is dropped rather than maintained — quipu-m9h; (2) the join is still quadratic because swapping SQL for hash lookups at the LEAF leaves eval_bgp's nested loop intact — quipu-att. Enable by default once both land.

Two invalidation bugs the suite caught, both from the write-time policy guard querying inside the savepoint: a denied write left the model holding rolled-back facts, and a model cached before staging made the guard deny a compliant write. Fixed by invalidating on entry to transact and on both exits.
close_reason: Complete and ON by default. eval_bgp hash-joins through the model for multi-pattern BGPs behind the scope guard. No measured regression on any query shape; 27x-310x on joins. Single-pattern BGPs deliberately stay on SQL (routing them through the model was a 0.12ms -> 320ms regression). Size bounded at 1M triples, checked with a COUNT. Differential test over 10 multi-pattern shapes plus the full 1020-test suite run with the model on.

title: Escalation precedent: attach nearest decided DecisionRequests to a newly minted request
description: docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md, Further applications #4. When the router mints a DecisionRequest, similarity-search prior DECIDED requests and attach the nearest as precedent — the human decider sees 'you rejected something similar, here is why', with the similarity scores on record so the precedent claim is falsifiable. Stage-1 advisory context under the identify-and-inform-before-refusing ordering; the ruling itself stays the human's. Corpus: decided request + decision records already in the store.
close_reason: mint_request attaches up to 3 nearest DECIDED requests as reified PrecedentLink nodes (precedentRequest + similarityScore + similarityMethod, shape-enforced together); only signed-decider decisions count (reuses decision_verifies); embedding-cosine similarity with honest method identity; degrades to no-precedent on missing/failing provider, never blocks minting. +15 tests, gate green (commit 9cbc747)

title: Claimed-linkage verification: similarity-check aegis:implements claims against the cited work item
description: docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md, Further applications #1. When a commit or bead-close claims to implement a work item, compare the diff/commit content's embedding against the cited item's description. Three outcomes: grounded / cited-but-dissimilar (fabricated linkage — the provenance edge becomes checkable rather than trusted) / no-citation. Verdict seals score, threshold, model identity, corpus watermark; advisory or escalate placement only; any recorded fact lands sourceKind=inferred. Unverified aegis:implements edges poison replay-derived rules — this closes that hole. Corpus: bobbin's beads index; consumes quipu-3aj's vocabulary.
close_reason: verify_claimed_linkage with typed outcomes Grounded / CitedButDissimilar / NoCitation / Unevaluated; evidence seals score, threshold, model identity, corpus watermark; aegis:linkageOutcome closed property + Verdict similarity-seal fields; aegis:implements declared; linkage.ttl catalog (must-ground, tier embedding, 0.75 threshold OperatingPoint, soft PAA warn). 3aj placement rules proven to cover it. +17 tests, gate green (commit 1589f18)

title: Entity-grounded predicate vocabulary: candidateSource, groundingQuery, must-ground/must-not-ground
description: docs/design/semantic-grounded-edit-policies.md (2026-08-15). Demote the ticket regex to candidate extractor; truth becomes membership in the graph's own work-item set via aegis:groundingQuery. Three-outcome evaluation (grounded / unresolvable-fabricated-reference / no-candidate); missing grounding projection = unevaluated, never satisfied. Add shapes + definition-time placement rules for the new match types. Sequencing step 1 of the design; yupana-side projection is a separate bead in the bobbin tracker. Also covers the model-tier follow-on (OperatingPoint nonzero tolerances required, PAA/escalate placement only) as step 4.
notes: Rev 2 of the design (same day): regex fully removed. Candidates are the introduced text's tokens (candidateSource 'token'); the id set alone defines ticket-shape. New Design B: embedding-similarity grounding against bobbin's beads index — tier 'embedding' (reproducible-but-approximate), verdict records matched item + score + threshold + model identity + corpus watermark, nonzero OperatingPoint, PAA/escalate only. Generative judgment demoted to Design C, last resort.
close_reason: Implemented: candidateSource + groundingQuery vocabulary in shapes (PredicateShape + aegis-properties.ttl), matchType extended with must-ground/must-not-ground, Predicate tier extended with tree-sitter+graph/embedding/model. Definition-time placement rules: grounded matchType requires groundingQuery; embedding/model-tier policies refused deny@PAG and required to carry a nonzero-FP OperatingPoint. v2 exemplar predicate in the treesitter catalog. 17 new tests, full gate green (commit 5eeea9e)

title: LIMIT pushdown and selectivity-ordered patterns
description:
Carried over from quipu-att, whose hash-join half has landed.

Two things remain:

1. LIMIT is not pushed down. 'SELECT ?s WHERE { ?s a <T> } LIMIT 100' is linear in store size (4.6ms at 1k episodes to 56ms at 10k) because the scan completes before the limit applies. Bounded queries should stop once they have enough rows.

2. Patterns are evaluated in source order. With the read model resident, index cardinalities are free — by_predicate(a).len() is a hash lookup — so a BGP can be ordered most-selective-first instead of trusting how the query was written. The hash join already picks the smaller side to BUILD from; this is about the order the patterns are folded in.

## Acceptance

The type scan is flat rather than linear across the scale_bench sizes. A pathological source ordering plans the same as a good one, with a test that writes the same join both ways and asserts comparable timing.
close_reason: Both halves landed. LIMIT pushdown: Slice installs a row cap through prefix-safe subtrees only (Project/Reduced); the BGP leaf stops the lazy SQL scan once enough rows BOUND. Type scan now flat: 0.51ms@1k -> 0.63ms@10k (was 100.21ms@10k); bounded 2-hop join 1050ms -> 566ms. Ordering: join_plan folds hash joins by measured cardinality (smallest, then connected-smallest, deterministic tie-break); pathological source order provably produces the same plan (unit test) and identical results (integration test). 5 new tests; full gate green.

title: Incrementally maintain the resident read model
description:
Store::read_model is DROPPED on every committed write and rebuilt on next use (246ms at 10k episodes). ReadModel::apply/apply_all already exist and are tested, so the machinery is there — but wiring them into the commit path needs care the first cut deliberately deferred.

The problem: a transact can close prior facts as a side effect of asserting new ones, and those closures are NOT in the caller's datum list. An incremental path must observe what the write actually DID, not what it was asked to do, or the model silently keeps facts the store has closed. That is the exact failure mode the whole design exists to avoid, which is why dropping — correct by construction — shipped first.

Likely shape: have the write path report the effective datum set (including closures) from inside the savepoint, and feed that to apply_all. Graph scoping matters too: apply only when the model's graph matches the write's target, else drop.

## Acceptance

The resident model survives a write without a rebuild, and a differential test writes a long mixed sequence (assert, re-assert changing a value, retract, tombstone, graph-scoped writes) asserting after EVERY step that the incrementally-maintained model equals a rebuilt one. Rebuild cost disappears from the write-then-read path.
notes:
INVESTIGATED — the effective datum set is precisely identifiable, and the bead's premise is confirmed:

1. staged_datums = the caller's datums PLUS owl_domain_range_inferences (src/store/ops.rs:225-231, under the owl feature).
2. supersede_functional_values (ops.rs:252) closes prior values for functional properties — implicit closures the caller never asked for.
3. close_assertion (ops.rs:265) fires ONLY for Op::Retract and closes the exact (e,a,v,g), so a plain assert does NOT implicitly close a prior value. That part is simpler than feared.
4. Idempotent asserts are skipped by check_exists (ops.rs:271); ReadModel::insert is idempotent too, so those already agree.
5. written_asserts (ops.rs:243) already collects 'datums ACTUALLY written' for the event log — that is very close to the set apply_all needs, and is the natural thing to thread out through Staged.

So the shape is: have stage_and_guard report the effective set (extend Staged, likely reusing written_asserts plus the supersession closures), apply it when graph == model.graph(), and drop otherwise. This touches the write path, which is the most correctness-sensitive code in the store, so it wants its own careful change rather than being folded into anything else.
close_reason: The write path now vouches for its complete change set when it can (Staged::effective), and the model is MAINTAINED rather than dropped. It cannot vouch when OWL inference extends the batch or functional supersede closes prior values via bulk UPDATE ... WHERE v != ? — those rebuild. A write to a different graph leaves a ROOT model untouched entirely. The structural enabler was suspending model consultation for the duration of a write instead of dropping it, which also retired both invalidation bugs.

title: Cache/scope graph::project() to a named graph
description:
Carried over from quipu-yez after its superlinearity claim was retracted (that was a cold-vs-warm measurement error; project() is linear).

What remains: project() is uncached and pays a full scan per call — 134.5ms warm at 10k episodes over ROOT. Against a small derived graph that is fine; against a large ROOT it will not be.

Scoping it to a named graph is likely small and composes with quipu-nip (per-graph read models), since both want the resident/scanned set to be the distilled layer rather than the episode log.

## Acceptance

project() can be scoped to a named graph. Repeat calls over an unchanged graph do not repeat the scan, or it is documented why caching is not worth it.
close_reason: project_in_graph scopes the scan to one named graph (unknown IRI refuses); project_cached memoizes the last projection on Store keyed by (graph, filters) and stamped with latest_tx_id, so repeat calls over an unchanged graph never repeat the scan. MCP tool + CLI gained a graph param; docs updated; 4 new tests; full gate green.

title: Bound the TermCache
description:
The TermCache added in quipu-yzf is unbounded — it grows to roughly the store's term count as reads touch terms. Measured ~350 bytes/term, so ~7MB at 30k terms (10k episodes) but several hundred MB for a 1M-episode raw log in a long-lived server process.

Fine at the scales the design targets (§7 argues the resident set should be the derived layer, not the episode log), but a server pinned to a large ROOT will accumulate the whole dictionary on the read path with no ceiling.

Options: an LRU with a configurable budget; or scope the cache alongside the per-graph read model (quipu-nip) so it is bounded by the same thing.

## Acceptance

Cache growth is bounded by configuration, with the default preserving today's behaviour at the sizes measured in docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §8 Phase 1. Eviction cannot produce a wrong answer — a miss re-reads from SQL.
close_reason: Bounded at DEFAULT_TERM_CACHE_LIMIT (500k terms, ~175MB at the measured 350 bytes/term), adjustable via Store::set_term_cache_limit; 0 disables caching and drops what is held. At the cap it refuses admission rather than evicting — every policy is correct since a miss reads SQL, and eviction under a full-dictionary scan just thrashes. 3 tests including that warm_term_cache respects the cap.

title: Export/import a .db from wasm, and pack round-trip
description:
The .db file stays the interchange format. rusqlite's serialize feature wraps sqlite3_serialize — hand it a connection, get the exact bytes of a .db file, hand those to a Blob, and it downloads. sqlite3_deserialize takes them back.

Packs should work as-is: src/pack.rs re-interns every fact through transact_to_graph rather than copying rows, so term ids and Value::Ref payloads are correct by construction and a browser-produced pack needs no remapping. That claim needs a test, not an assumption. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §6, §8 Phase 4.

## Acceptance

A store serialized in wasm opens in the `quipu` CLI and in sqlite3 unchanged. A pack produced in a browser attaches to a native store. Round-trip test in CI.
notes: Update 2026-08-13: quipu-qd2 landed, so this is next in the chain. rusqlite 0.40 (now in-tree) exposes the serialize feature the design names; the wasm/harness worker + Playwright driver is the natural place for the browser half of the round-trip test.
close_reason: Landed. Store::serialize_db / Store::open_from_bytes (rusqlite serialize feature) plus pack_to_bytes sharing the whole build with pack() via the extracted pack_into. Acceptance verified by just wasm roundtrip (wasm/harness/roundtrip.mjs): a store serialized in a tab opens in the quipu CLI with the type scan intact row-for-row (sqlite3 leg runs where the CLI exists; the same engine's integrity_check is pinned in a native unit test); a pack produced in a browser — object-position Ref included — respaces, attaches to a native store, hash-verifies and answers a GRAPH query (examples/attach_pack_check.rs); and the reverse direction, a native .db's bytes opening in a tab. One real bug found and fixed: SQLite refuses to deserialize a WAL-format image and native stores run WAL, so open_from_bytes normalizes header bytes 18/19 (the journal_mode=DELETE edit, valid for a checkpointed db) — pinned by the_bytes_of_a_wal_mode_file_import_cleanly. The 'round-trip test in CI' leg rides quipu-ame (the CI matrix bead, which this bead blocks): the workflow there should run just wasm test + just wasm roundtrip.

title: Event-log retention policy
description:
Measured via dbstat on a 10k-episode store: the events table plus its two indexes is 25.2MB of an 83.3MB database — 30.3%. The log is durable with no expiry by design (the reactor-down-6wk fix), which is correct for a server with consumers and pure overhead for a deployment that has none. A knowledge pack exported for a browser carries no consumers at all.

Needs a retention policy that does not break the durable-replay guarantee for consumers that DO exist. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §5.1.

## Acceptance

Retention is configurable, defaults to today's behaviour (no expiry), and a consumer's committed offset is never invalidated by retention. Storage reduction measured on a 10k-episode store.
close_reason: Store::prune_events deletes by age, never past MIN(committed_offset) over registered consumers; opt-in via [quipu.events] retention_days (default unset = keep forever, today's behaviour); server prunes hourly when configured. Measured on the 10k-episode store: 83.3MB -> 53.5MB after VACUUM (35.8% reduction, 100,012 events). Docs: wasm-support §5.1 note + book configuration page.

title: Selectivity-ordered join planning and LIMIT pushdown
description:
With the ReadModel resident, index cardinalities are known without a round-trip, so BGP patterns can be ordered most-selective-first instead of source order. Separately, LIMIT is not pushed down today: the type scan `?s a <Service> LIMIT 100` is linear in store size (2.8ms at 500 episodes rising to 145.9ms at 20k) because the scan completes before the limit applies.

Design: docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §8 Phase 4.

## Acceptance

BGP patterns are evaluated in selectivity order, with a test showing a pathological source ordering now plans the same as the good one. Bounded queries stop scanning the whole store: the type scan is flat rather than linear across the scale_bench sizes.
close_reason: Hash join implemented in eval_bgp: each pattern evaluated once and joined on shared variables, smaller side built. Turns the 2-hop join linear — 27x to 310x faster (173,803ms -> 560ms at 10k episodes). LIMIT pushdown and selectivity ORDERING remain, refiled.

title: Trim fact indexes and timestamp encoding
description:
Measured via dbstat at 10k episodes: the facts table is 10.0MB and its indexes (idx_eavt, idx_aevt, idx_vaet, idx_geav, idx_tx, sqlite_autoindex) are 34.5MB — 3.4x the data. Separately, valid_from/valid_to are ISO-8601 TEXT at ~20 bytes each where an integer would be 8.

Both are load-bearing decisions that predate the measurement, so this is an investigation before it is a change: establish which permutations actually earn their keep under real query mixes. Changing the timestamp encoding is a migration and touches the bitemporal core — scope carefully. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §5.1.

## Acceptance

Index usage measured under a representative query mix, with a recommendation per permutation. Any index removal keeps the full suite green and records the storage delta. Timestamp re-encoding is scoped as its own bead if pursued, not smuggled in here.
close_reason: Closed

title: Portability shims: time, fs, getrandom
description:

Needs a quipu::time shim over Date/performance.now.

getrandom 0.2 (via ring) and 0.3 both need their js/wasm_js features PLUS RUSTFLAGS='--cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js"'. Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §4.4, §8 Phase 2.

Route std::time/std::fs through a shim in the same change that lands the qd2 [patch], where CI can actually build it.

title: Per-graph read models scoped to the derived layer
description:
At ~350 bytes/fact, 1M raw episodes would be ~6GB resident — beyond wasm32's 4GB address space entirely and heavy for a server. That is the design telling us what the model should contain: episodes are raw ingest, the valuable artifact is the DERIVED graph, and Quipu already produces it (src/reasoner/ writes affects/dependsOn with reasoner:<rule-id> provenance; graph.rs Louvain with persist:true writes quipu:memberOfCommunity; src/derivation.rs records recompute recipes).

Scope the read model per named graph so the resident set is the distilled layer while the episode log stays in SQLite, queried rarely by anchored walks and time travel — the shapes that are already fast or already need SQL. This also makes the GRAPH <iri> case work rather than fall back (see rm3).

Design: docs/design/in-memory-read-model.md §7, §8 Phase 5.

## Acceptance

A read model can be built for a single named graph. Resident cost for a derived-layer graph is measured and recorded. A store with a large ROOT and a small derived graph holds only the derived graph resident.
close_reason: Closed

title: SQLite VFS for wasm via sqlite-wasm-rs
description:
The one hard build blocker. `libsqlite3-sys` with `bundled` compiles SQLite's C through cc, and wasm32-unknown-unknown has no libc: `sqlite3/sqlite3.c:14884:10: fatal error: 'stdio.h' file not found`. Everything Quipu is sits on that connection.

Route: sqlite-wasm-rs as a libsqlite3-sys-compatible shim via [patch] — memory VFS first, OPFS second. OPFS is the real target: the memory VFS requires the database to fit in linear memory, which is fine for a distilled pack and hopeless for the episode log.

(The alternative, a wasi-sdk sysroot on wasm32-wasip1, is viable — libsqlite3-sys's build.rs already special-cases wasi and ships wasm32-wasi-vfs.c — but targets wasmtime, not a browser tab.) Design: docs/design/wasm-support.md §4.2, §8 Phase 3.

## Acceptance

`cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` succeeds. A store opens, ingests and queries under both the memory VFS and OPFS. Data survives a page reload under OPFS.
notes:
Triage 2026-08-12: needs the wasm32-unknown-unknown target plus a browser (acceptance includes OPFS persistence across a page reload) — not feasible in the current container. quipu-gsg landed the clock shim and fs gating this depends on; the [patch] route via sqlite-wasm-rs remains the plan.

Triage 2026-08-13: CORRECTION — feasible in the remote container after all. Headless Chromium 141 + Playwright 1.56 are preinstalled, wasm32-unknown-unknown installs (static.rust-lang.org is proxy-open), and OPFS FileSystemSyncAccessHandle write -> page reload -> read -> browser relaunch -> read was verified by probe on 2026-08-13. Harness recipe: docs/design/wasm-support.md §9 (Playwright persistent-context for the reload acceptance; wasm-pack test with a --disable-build-check chromedriver wrapper for the unit suite).

Acceptance all green in the wasm/harness Playwright harness (just wasm test): cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features succeeds; store opens, ingests 50 episodes (1000 triples) and answers the three scale_bench reads under BOTH the memory VFS and OPFS (opfs-sahpool via sqlite-wasm-vfs, registered as default VFS by the embedder — no quipu code knows wasm exists); OPFS data survives a page reload AND a full browser relaunch. Full native suite green (1058 passed) — upgrade cost was one progress_handler Result. Measured caveat recorded in wasm-support.md §4.2: journal_mode=WAL degrades to delete on both wasm VFS.

title: graph::project() is superlinear and uncached
description:
Measured: 118ms at 1k episodes, 745ms at 4k, 2768ms at 10k — roughly O(n^1.3), and paid per call with no caching. Against a small derived graph that is fine; against ROOT it will not be. Part of the superlinearity is the per-fact store.resolve() round-trips that rm1 removes; measure again after rm1 before doing anything else.

Scoping it to a named graph is likely a small change and composes with rm5.

## Acceptance

Re-measured after rm1 lands. If still superlinear, the cause is identified. project() can be scoped to a named graph.
notes: Refiled bead is quipu-tz5, not quipu-8em — ID corrected.
close_reason: NOT superlinear — the finding was a measurement error on my part. The 118/745/2768ms figures were COLD (first touch of an 83MB file); warm, project() is 13.0/24.2/48.5/134.5ms at 1k/2k/4k/10k episodes, which is linear (1.86x, 2.00x, 2.77x for 2x, 2x, 2.5x the data) and ~20x faster than published. project() does not resolve per fact, so the term cache was not the cause either. Design doc corrected in place. What remains true is that it is UNCACHED and paid per call, and that scoping it to a named graph composes with quipu-nip — refiled as quipu-8em.

title: quipu: the context pipeline truncates silently, so a partial answer is indistinguishable from a complete one
description:
src/context/mod.rs truncates twice with no counter — at :222 (entities, to max_entities) and :281 (facts, to max_facts_per_entity). KnowledgeSummary (:68) reports total_entities, total_facts, direct_hits, linked_additions and an EmbeddingStatus, all of which describe what was RETURNED; nothing describes what was dropped. A caller receiving 20 entities cannot tell whether the graph held 20 or 2000.

This repo already implements the honest version elsewhere: src/graph_view.rs:239-245 returns `truncated: {shown, of, edges_shown, edges_of}` and deliberately drops the periphery first so the truncation is at least principled. EmbeddingStatus itself was added (quipu #53) for exactly this class of reason — an empty entities list was ambiguous between 'nothing matched' and 'no provider attached', and the answer had to travel with the result rather than sit in a log the caller cannot see. The same argument applies to omission.

FIX: carry omission counts on KnowledgeSummary, following the graph_view convention, and populate them at both truncation sites.

WHY NOW: yupana's work-item briefing and bobbin's context injection both build on this pipeline and both need to tell an agent how much it is not being shown. bobbin drops files and reports only to stderr; yupana's advise-mode advisory goes to systemMessage. All three report omission to a channel the model cannot read; this is the graph-side half.

ACCEPTANCE: a query whose candidate set exceeds the caps reports the true totals; one that fits reports equal shown/of rather than omitting the field.
notes: Found 2026-08-18 while planning progressive disclosure across quipu/yupana/bobbin.
close_reason: Done. KnowledgeSummary carries `truncated` at both truncation sites, following graph_view's existing convention rather than a second one. The shape is deliberately NOT shown/of: entities_considered is what was GATHERED, more_available says the WALK stopped because the budget filled, and per-entity fact totals stay uncounted (LIMIT max+1 answers 'is there more' for one extra row rather than costing a COUNT per entity). The first draft did report a total; its own test caught that link expansion breaks at the budget, making the count a floor presented as a ceiling — the same overclaim one layer up from the one being fixed.

title: quipu: add the work-item disclosure rungs to the quipu_ask catalog
description:
Progressive disclosure needs a small pushed briefing whose census names REAL, parameter-validated calls that expand each section. src/mcp/named_query.rs is the right home — the catalog is already self-describing (rendered as JSON for discovery) and validates params, which is what makes an advertised handle trustworthy rather than a promise.

What exists already and should be reused, not duplicated: entity_facts, service_deps, references_to, entities_of_type, labeled_like, and — directly on point for work items — entity_work ('work-items and commits that touched a code entity') and cochanged_with, both added under quipu#37 over the Bead <-aegis:implements- GitCommit -aegis:modifies-> entity chain. quipu_cooccurrence covers the work-item-to-work-item direction bitemporally.

FIX: add the missing rungs keyed on a work item — brief_ground, brief_similar, brief_central — plus a narrow entity_summary that reuses build_node_result (src/mcp/search.rs:208), which is already the compact {iri, label, types, summary, score} shape. Each takes a limit and reports what it omitted.

CARRY PLANE AND TRUST ON THE RESULT. camayoc's planes rank crew:declared (30) > crew:records (20) > crew:inferred (0), with the 20-to-0 gap deliberate, and its competency suite asks directly (crew-task-lifecycle.md Q14) what knowledge would vanish under a high-trust floor. A rung that returns 4 items without saying three are inferred flattens the quarantine that plane labelling exists to enforce.

NOTE the caveat already in named_query.rs: these provenance queries return nothing until the modifies/implements edges are populated. That ingress is camayoc's git adapter.

ACCEPTANCE: each new rung appears in the discovery catalog with described params; counts agree with what a briefing census advertises.
notes: The briefing side is tracked in bobbin's tracker as the yupana disclosure-ladder bead.
close_reason: Done: brief_ground, brief_related and entity_summary, all walking the existing implements/modifies chain with no new vocabulary. They are in the catalog rather than in bespoke tools precisely so a briefing census can name them and have the promise hold — one test asserts registration rather than trusting it. entity_summary is asserted NOT to select arbitrary predicates, or it is entity_facts under another name and the ladder has one rung.

title: quipu: /query serialization makes the edit guard fail open on 5.2% of edits
description:
Measured 2026-08-04 and recorded in yupana/docs/book/src/reference/policy-guard.md:120-146 and yupana/src/hook/rule_planes.rs:206-217: 5.2% of all pre-edit guard invocations — 19% on one day — failed open on projection timeouts, because quipu serves /query effectively one at a time while every agent edit issues one.

yupana mitigated its side with a durable projection cache (a cache-served verdict enforces but is marked STALE and states its age, and past the TTL the cache is refused and the guard fails open LOUDLY). That is the right client-side behaviour and it does not address the cause.

The cause is here: a single-flight /query path under concurrent agent load. Every fail-open is an edit that passed unguarded, so this is a policy-availability defect, not a latency nicety.

WORTH INVESTIGATING: whether the serialization is the store lock, the SPARQL engine, or the axum handler; whether a read-only concurrent path is available; and whether the projection could be served by one query rather than the five (POLICY_QUERY, TEXT_POLICY_QUERY, GROUNDED_POLICY_QUERY, WORK_ITEM_SCOPE_QUERY, GROUNDING_SET_QUERY) yupana currently issues per refresh.

ACCEPTANCE: concurrent /query load from N clients does not serialize; the measured guard fail-open rate under fleet load drops materially and is re-measured rather than assumed.
notes: Filed from the yupana side 2026-08-18. The client-side mitigation is already shipped; this is the server-side cause.
close_reason:
ALREADY FIXED, verified 2026-08-18 by reading the code rather than by re-measuring. /query takes a POOLED READ (`store.read()`, src/server/base.rs), not the writer's mutex, backed by a read pool of 4 read-only connections by default (config.rs:405, built at src/server.rs:296-340). The one-at-a-time behaviour the 2026-08-04 measurement recorded predates that pool; the handler's own comment describes the before/after curve, so this was fixed and the bead was filed from the yupana side against a stale symptom.

TWO CONDITIONS STILL DISABLE THE POOL, and both are announced rather than silent:
  * an in-memory store — each `:memory:` connection is a separate empty database, so a pool would serve reads from nothing;
  * a configured vector delegate or local vector backend — the backends are boxed trait objects and are not Clone, so a pooled reader would answer vector search from the built-in SQLite table while the writer answered from the configured backend. Same question, two answers, no error. The code refuses to build the pool and says so.

So the remaining exposure is narrow and known: a deployment that turns LanceDB on gets serialised reads back, and with it yupana's fail-open rate. That is worth a fresh bead with that framing if and when lancedb is enabled — it is a different problem from the one this bead describes, and filing it now would be speculating about a configuration nobody runs (`lancedb: false` today).

title: golden-paths: conformance grammar v1 - the versioned step-matching contract shared with yupana
description: docs/design/golden-paths-blessing.md section 4 and yupana docs/golden-path-guard.md FR-40/FR-41 both require it: the definition of 'trajectory T conforms to path P' (v1: action kind + target type per step, in order, gaps allowed) must be ONE versioned contract consumed by both the backtest and the live guard, or backtest-justified promotions and live verdicts drift apart invisibly. Deliver: the grammar spec (a design doc section or schema file), a version identifier carried by every projected path, backtest report, and conformance verdict, and refusal of a grammar version a consumer does not implement (reported as unevaluated, never silently skipped).
close_reason: gp-grammar/1 specified in docs/design/conformance-grammar.md (version scheme, carry/refuse rules, serialization) and implemented in src/path/grammar.rs; the backtest carries the version on every report. The guard-side carry/refuse lands with yupana FR-40/41, which the spec binds from their first cut.

title: golden-paths: quipu path cone - the provenance-cone pruning report, built on speculate
description: docs/design/golden-paths-blessing.md section 3. Given a Trajectory whose steps carry derivation edges to their outputs, compute which steps the terminal falsifier-gated Verification's derivation chain depends on: speculatively remove step S (Store::speculate in src/store/ops.rs, speculate_remove in src/impact.rs); if the chain survives, S is out-of-cone and mechanically prunable. CLI `quipu path cone <trajectory>` + MCP. Output stored as facts on the candidate, each omission carrying its authority tag (cone-analysis vs a human Decision IRI) so competency Q5/Q6 stay answerable. A trajectory without derivation edges reports CANNOT EVALUATE for its steps - degrading toward human ruling, never toward guessing.
close_reason: quipu path cone + quipu_path_cone MCP + POST /path/cone (ro). Forward reachability over the impact BFS, per-step in-cone/out-of-cone/cannot-evaluate, refusal without steps or falsifier-gated verification. Design corrected in golden-paths-blessing.md: speculative removal was unsound (a load-bearing step could read prunable via artifact-owned edges); the bead's 'output stored as facts' lands at draft time via quipu path draft. 17 module tests; full suite 1170 green; just check green.

title: golden-paths: quipu path backtest - trajectory-exemplar backtest over bitemporal history
description: docs/design/golden-paths-blessing.md section 4: generalize the src/governance/backtest.rs pattern from single-edit exemplars to trajectories. Given a candidate path, replay over recorded history: N work items would have matched applicability (deterministic core: work-item type + topic entities); conformers' vs non-conformers' done rates; divergence points. Distinguish 0 hits from cannot-evaluate, exactly as the existing backtest does. Cites the conformance grammar version (quipu-gp1). The report is what a human promotes on - it must be storable as promotion evidence (competency Q8/Q13).
close_reason: quipu path backtest + quipu_path_backtest MCP + POST /path/backtest. Applicability = shared work-item topic (deterministic core only), gp-grammar/1 subsequence matching, conformers/deviators done-rates with cannot-evaluate kept apart, refusal of uncompilable patterns and unbounded populations. Report carries the grammar version (quipu-gp1 carry rule).

title: golden-paths: path drafting born-advisory - generalize the policy-by-example scaffold
description: docs/design/golden-paths-blessing.md section 5: a candidate that survives cone-pruning and backtest is drafted like an exemplar policy (src/governance/draft.rs): born advisory, effect warn hard-coded, exemplar Trajectories cited via aegis:exemplar so any warn/deny answers 'because this concrete work succeeded this way'. Promotion rides the EXISTING advisory-to-enforcing gates with conformance events as traffic - no parallel promotion machinery. Demotion is aegis:supersededBy. L5 (path-derived authorization) stays out of scope until verdict signing exists.
close_reason: quipu path draft emits GoldenPath + PathOmission Turtle for human review, never writing - the governance draft.rs posture. Mechanical omissions cite cone-analysis; every human cut requires its Decision IRI; CannotEvaluate steps are never silently cut; dead ends preserved. Born a candidate: no promotion is drafted, and promotion rides the existing gates unchanged, so nothing enforces before advisory.

title: fork-at-any-event: make speculate a first-class named fork with structural diff (ActiveGraph's ergonomics)
description: Proposal from the ActiveGraph comparison (Nakajima, 'The Log is the Agent: Event-Sourced Reactive Graphs for Auditable, Forkable Agentic Systems', arXiv:2605.21997; companion: 'Regimes', arXiv:2606.10241). Quipu already holds the pieces - Store::speculate is closure-scoped and uncommitted, and bitemporal replay (unravel) reads any past state - but there is no PERSISTENT, NAMED fork: fork the store at any transaction into an independent lineage, query it exactly like the main line, diff it structurally against main or another fork, then discard or promote. ActiveGraph demonstrates fork->test->promote as a one-liner UX and its value for hypothesis testing over nondeterministic agent runs. Our consumers: the golden-path pipeline (backtest/what-if under counterfactual histories - 'would this candidate path have conformed if X had gone differently'), promotion evidence, and incident archaeology. Constraint to state up front: a promoted fork re-enters through the write gates (SHACL + policy) - fork ergonomics must never become a gate bypass; the evidence bar is the thing ActiveGraph does not have and we do not give up. Sketch: quipu fork <tx> [--name n]; --fork n on read/query; quipu fork diff <a> <b>; quipu fork drop|promote.

title: quipu:distinctFrom is instructed by the strict-mode refusal but does not exist
description: strict_mode refuses a write and tells the caller "Use an existing IRI or assert quipu:distinctFrom to override" (src/episode/mod.rs), and src/config.rs documents that override on the strict_mode field. The term exists nowhere else: no namespace constant, no entry in ontologies/ or shapes/, no read path anywhere in src/. It is a string inside the sentence that recommends it. So a strict refusal names an escape hatch nothing honours, and the only actual escape is setting strict_mode = false, which drops the check for EVERY entity rather than the one pairing the writer meant to excuse. docs/design/entity-resolution.md compounds it with a status banner claiming strict_mode / quipu:distinctFrom are "present" and were "exercised live in production". Fix: mint the term and honour it, per-pairing, as a durable fact so the override survives the write that declared it (a re-ingest that has to re-declare would be refused the moment a producer forgot). Alternative considered and rejected: delete the promise from the message and document strict mode as all-or-nothing. Found by doc-vs-code review, 2026-08-21.

title: Entity resolution reads main.facts, so it cannot see attached layers and silently under-reports
description: resolve_by_name prepared `SELECT e, v FROM facts ...` — the bare table, which is main.facts. The composed read source is Store::facts_source() (the UNION ALL built by attach::build_facts_source), and resolution never consulted it. On the deployment docs/design/multi-db-composition.md is explicitly designed for — a shared reference layer or knowledge pack attached beside a per-tenant store — resolving a name the LAYER already defines returns zero candidates and the tenant mints a duplicate of the entity it attached the pack in order to share. That is the fragmentation resolution exists to prevent, failing precisely in the composition case, and failing silently: no candidates is indistinguishable from no duplicates. Second half of the same bug: the predicate id comes from store.lookup(), which is main-scoped, and a layer interns rdfs:label in its own term space — so even against the union an `a = ?` predicate selects none of the layer's rows. lookup_all (#76) is the existing answer. Third: the VECTOR half cannot be fixed the same way. `vectors` is per-database and an attached pack may carry a different embedding model or dimension, so unioning the indexes would turn a working search into the dimension-mismatch error src/vector.rs raises deliberately. Report the scope on every result instead, so a caller can tell an empty list that means "no duplicates" from one that means "the layer was never searched". Found 2026-08-21.

title: Episode nodes resolve one at a time, so contention between them is invisible
description: ingest_episode_with_resolution looped over episode.nodes calling resolve_entity per node, each resolution blind to the others. When two nodes of one write both top-match the same existing entity, advisory mode emits two hints pointing at one IRI — which reads as two independent near-misses — and strict mode refuses whichever node came first in the list and says nothing about the other. The write is about to fragment one entity into several and no field says so, which is the case where the caller most needs to be told. Fix: resolve a write in one pass and report entities that are the TOP candidate for more than one node (top, not any: two nodes can resemble a third entity without either claiming to be it, and reporting that as conflict trains callers to ignore the field). Explicitly NOT a stable matching, and the reason is worth recording because the question recurs: Gale-Shapley guarantees no blocking pair rather than maximum total match quality, and is proposer-optimal, so with one symmetric similarity score there is no principled proposing side and the asymmetry would be arbitrary; max-weight bipartite (Hungarian) is the right algorithm if this ever does assign. More fundamentally, assigning is a judgment made from a score the caller can see and quipu cannot justify, and quipu stores facts and leaves judgments to the reader. Detect and report; never resolve. Raised by Stiwi, 2026-08-21.

title: Resolution is O(nodes x labels): the label scan sits inside the per-node loop
description: resolve_by_name full-scans every current rdfs:label fact and, per row, decodes the value blob, runs strsim::jaro_winkler and calls store.resolve() — and it ran once PER NODE, plus one store.embed_query per node. A 20-node episode against a 50k-label store is a million Jaro-Winkler comparisons and 20 embedding round-trips where one scan and 50k comparisons would do. The rows do not change during a resolution pass, so the scan is hoistable: build the label index once for the whole batch, compare N times. Resolve id->IRI lazily, only for rows that clear the threshold, since most labels match nothing and resolve is a query per id. Depends on quipu-er3 — both want the per-node loop restructured into gather-then-decide, and landing them independently means the second conflicts with the first. Correctness claim for the refactor is that it changes nothing else: same candidates, same order, as the single-entity path. Found 2026-08-21.
